Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Precision Surgical Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Michael Reynolds, CEO; Jennifer Hale, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Precision Surgical Systems demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance. We'll start with hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates, then move to inventory management and working capital optimization, FDA approvals and CE marks obtained, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and year, and finally organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Jennifer will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Lisa will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. This metric reflects procedural demand, site-of-care shifts, and the strength of our razor-and-blade model, where recurring revenue from instruments, accessories, and service contracts now makes up 68% of total sales, up from 62% a year ago.

Overall, our adoption rate—the percentage of qualified sites actively using our PrecisionNav and RoboFlex systems—hit 82% across our targeted U.S. footprint of more than 4,200 hospitals and ASCs. That's a 14% increase year-over-year and 3% sequentially from Q2.

In hospitals, which represent 72% of our installed base, we reached 88% adoption among top academic medical centers and community hospitals. We placed 47 new systems this quarter, growing our U.S. hospital base to 1,856 units, up 12% year-over-year. Utilization averaged 22.5 procedures per system per month, up 8%, thanks to our Gen-3 software upgrade that improves OR efficiency by 25% with AI instrument tracking and haptic feedback.

We saw a 19% jump in repeat placements, with 65% of new hospital deals as multi-system expansions. Customers like Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic have expanded to over 15 systems each, praising our precision in partial knee replacements and spinal fusions, which cuts revision rates by up to 18% according to peer-reviewed data in the Journal of Bone & Joint Surgery.

U.S. hospital adoption stands at 91%, helped by CMS reimbursement boosts under the 2024 OPPS rule, up 4.2% for robotic ortho. Europe is at 76%, with momentum in Germany and the UK after CE Mark for our RoboFlex cardiac module—32 new placements, including a 10-system NHS deal. APAC is at 62% but picking up, with full China approvals expected Q1 2025 to challenge players like Tinavi.

Hospital capex caution has lengthened sales cycles to 9-12 months in some IDNs, but our FlexLease program, used in 40% of deals, converted 28% of pilots to adoptions.

ASCs tell an even stronger story, with adoption surging to 64%—a 32% year-over-year leap, now 28% of placements. We added 112 sites, reaching 892 systems, with volumes at 18.2 procedures per system monthly, exceeding hospitals due to single-use FlexTips cutting prep by 35%.

This tracks the outpatient shift: U.S. ASC volumes in urology, gynecology, and general surgery rose 22% per SG2 data, triple inpatient growth. CMS's expanded CPL with 60 new codes lifts reimbursements, like $8,500 for robotic hysterectomies versus $6,200 inpatient.

Our ASC Accelerator Program offers training, revenue optimization, and guarantees, converting 92% of demos. Wins include a 25-center USPI partnership and Regent expansions. Robotic prostatectomies achieve 95% same-day discharge, lifting ASC EBITDA 15-20%.

U.S. ASCs are at 72%, led by Texas and Florida's CON relaxations—Texas alone 28% of Q3 placements. Europe at 48%, growing 45% YoY in Italy and Spain post mini-OR cert. India at 35% via Apollo partnerships, saving 22% per procedure versus open surgery.

Our R&D backs this, with 40% pipeline fill. PrecisionNav 4.0's 4K visualization and AR overlays boosted conversions 27%. Single-port RoboFlex XP in FDA IDE trials targets ASCs with smaller footprint and $1.2M ASP.

We're gaining on Intuitive's da Vinci with 15% lower instruments and OR interoperability, plus 98.7% uptime winning 62% of evaluations against Medtronic Hugo and J&J Ottava.

We expect ASC adoption to 75% year-end, 85% 2025, at 11% CAGR versus 7% hospitals, driving higher utilization to 25 procedures by 2026 and steady $2,100 ASPs. We've dual-sourced FlexTips for 110% 2025 supply and announced $250M buyback, 15% R&D hike.

This validates our role in the $28B robotics market.

Now, let's talk about inventory management and working capital optimization. In med devices, balancing capital like robotic systems with consumables like stents and implants demands precision amid long lead times for titanium and polymers, FDA hurdles, and consignment shifts like Stryker's model.

We cut Days Inventory Outstanding 18% to 92 days from 112, beating industry 105-day median per Boston Scientific and Abbott benchmarks. Turns rose to 4.0x from 3.3x on a $428M base, down 12% YoY despite 9% revenue growth to $2.1B. Cash Conversion Cycle shortened 22 days to 28, freeing $145M for R&D and resilience.

Sequentially steady amid MediPulse defibrillator ramp post-ACC updates. Working capital to sales fell to 15.2% from 18.7%, lifting FCF to 115% of EBITDA above S&P average.

AI demand sensing with SAP and Palantir hit 92% SKU accuracy for just-in-time on catheters amid 7% nitinol inflation. RFID/IoT in 85% of 12 DCs cut shrinkage to 0.3%, tracking 28% ortho consignment up from 22%.

VMI with DuPont and TSMC stretched DPO to 68 days, diversifying rare earths 40% to SE Asia/Mexico.

U.S. (52% inventory) DIO 85 days via IDN consignment. Europe (28%) 105 days on IVDR but 20% excess cut via kanban. APAC (15%) 75 days supporting 30% electrophys growth.

This sets us for 85-day DIO year-end, 4.3x turns, $80-100M more cash. With net debt/EBITDA 1.8x, it funds robotics amid M&A like J&J Abiomed.

It's our moat in 8-10% growth industry.

Moving on to FDA approvals and CE marks obtained. Regulatory wins unlock markets in PMA and MDR worlds.

Q3 highlights: FDA 510(k) for OmniFlex peripheral stent with bioresorbable coating cutting restenosis 35%, 92% patency vs. 78% for Boston's Ranger, eyeing $4.2B PAD market at 7.8% CAGR.

PMA for NeuroPulse DBS rechargeable, MRI-conditional with AI sensing, reducing replacements 40%. LANDMARK study: 68% tremor reduction vs. 55% Abbott benchmark, $25M initial orders lifting neuro guidance to $450M, up 18%.

CE Mark MDR Class III for CardioGuard TAVR with tissue matrix vs. Edwards Sapien calcification, opening €2.8B Europe at 25% penetration.

U.S. 510(k) averaged 120 days, 22% faster. Europe 85% first-pass via €50M Galway hub.

$320M incremental FY24 revenue, 250bps margin to 68%. Four more clearances year-end, Shonin for Japan.

Our RegTech AI cuts prep 30%, 14 YTD approvals vs. 9 average for 15-20% EPS edge.

Next, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. R&D is our growth engine amid inflation and reimbursement shifts, targeting 12-15% CAGR segments.

Q3 spend $285M, 13.2% of $2.16B revenue—18% up, 120bps higher, above 10-11% peer average. Nine months $812M, 12-13% FY guide, 16% five-year CAGR, 28 programs up from 24.

40% or $114M to cardio: EvoFlow TAVR pivotal complete, 98% success, Q1 2025 data for 15-20% market expansion.

30% or $85.5M ortho/robotics: RoboOrtho full U.S. launch post-510(k), 25% less time vs. da Vinci, 22% Q3 revenue up, $40M Phase II AI module vs. Stryker Mako.

30% neuromod/digital: NeuroPulse DBS pivotal, 35% UPDRS gain, H2 2025 FDA.

U.S. 55% spend, 3 IDEs, EvoFlow breakthrough. Europe 25%, two CE Marks MDR-clear. APAC 15%, Shanghai hub for China ortho. Emerging 5% cost-optimized.

Personalized med with Illumina, 25% recyclable materials. 2.5x ROI past decade.

FY25 milestones: EvoFlow data, RoboOrtho AI, NeuroPulse IDE, wearable first-in-human, $1.2-1.5B by 2027, $4B NPV.

Maintains 12-13% spend.

Then, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. Capital like Horizon Imaging and Precision Robotics plants seeds; consumables like endoscopes, stents, catheters harvest.

Q3 revenue $1.25B, up 12% reported, 14% CC. Capital 34% or $425M, flat seq, +2% YoY. Consumables 66% $825M, +18% YoY, +5% seq—400bps shift, margins 68.5% blended, 75% consumables vs. 52% capital.

Installed base: 4,250 Horizon, 1,800 robotics, up 11%. Robotics utilization 82%, $1.2M TTM consumables pull-through to $1.5M with Gen-3.

U.S. 52% revenue, consumables +22% 69% mix on ASC boom. Europe 28%, consumables +14% 62% mix, capital -5% pricing. Emerging 20%, consumables +28% 72% mix, China VBP tender.

To 70% consumables FY26: Ecosystem bundles, $180M R&D nanomaterials, GE co-dev.

Q4 consumables 16-18%, capital mid-single.

Now, revenue and margin guidance for next quarter/year. Q4 $1.22-1.27B, 8-13% reported, 9-14% organic, up from prior.

Cardio 42% mix 12-17% organic on EvoFlow >50k implants. Ortho/spine 28% 7-11% AI Mako. Neuro/diabetes 18% 5-9% MiniStim/EvoPump. Endoscopy flat-4%.

U.S. 62% 11-15%, Europe 22% 4-8%, China/APAC 10% 10-14%, emerging 6% double-digit.

FY25 $4.95-5.05B, 7-10% reported, 8-11% organic, $50M FX headwind.

Gross 68.5-69.5% Q4, 68-69% FY, 50-100bps up on mix/supply. Op margin Q4 24.5-25.5%, FY 24-25%, EPS $4.85-4.95.

Innovate/expand/optimize: 20% new products, 500 ASCs, $200M LEAN savings.

Risks: elections, procedures, semis; upside China/EvoPump.

Finally, organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Q3 7.4%, FY 8.2% CC, all organic.

Cardio 38% 9.8% Q4, 10.2% FY: structural heart +15% Evolut PRO+, 120bps share.

Neuroscience 25% 8.5%: DBS +12% Percept PC.

Diabetes 22% 6.7%: MiniMed 780G +18% APAC.

MedSurg 15% 7.2%: endoscopy +11% GI Genius, Hugo +14%.

U.S. 52% 9.1%, electives 105% 2019. EMEA 24% 6.8%, APAC 18% 11.4% China/Japan. LATAM/Canada 6% 5.2%.

Innovation, commercial, supply pillars. FY24 guide 7-8%.

I will now turn the call over to Jennifer for a review of our financial results.

Jennifer Hale:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter. Q3 revenue was $2.1 billion, up 12% reported and 14% organic, driven by the trends Michael outlined. Gross margins expanded 150 basis points to 68.2% on consumables mix and efficiencies. Adjusted operating income rose 18% to $520 million, with EPS of $1.25, beating consensus. Expenses were disciplined: SG&A at 32% of revenue, R&D 13%. We generated $280 million operating cash flow, ending with $1.8 billion cash, net debt 1.8x EBITDA.

For FY24, revenue $8.2-8.3 billion, 9-10% organic; op margin 24.5%. Q4 as guided.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Jennifer. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of PrecisionNav 4.0 and RoboFlex XP is progressing well, and we anticipate they will revolutionize surgical precision and outpatient care.

Building on Michael's R&D overview, our pipeline is robust with 28 programs. Key progress includes EvoFlow TAVR enrollment complete, RoboOrtho launched with strong early data, and NeuroPulse advancing. We're allocating resources to AI enhancements and neuromodulation, with regional hubs accelerating global approvals. This supports our innovation leadership against peers.

Next, Lisa with insights on our commercial strategy.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Raj. Our commercial team has been instrumental in driving adoption of our products. We are focused on expanding our market presence and enhancing customer engagement.

Leveraging Michael's adoption details, we've secured key ASC partnerships like USPI, NHS deals, and China tenders. Our Accelerator Program and FlexLease have boosted conversions. Regionally, U.S. ASCs and APAC growth are priorities, with digital tools improving sales productivity 18%. We're gaining share in robotics and consumables through ecosystem bundles and competitive wins.

Now, back to Michael for Q&A.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee - JPMorgan:
Thanks. Michael, on the ASC adoption surge to 64%, can you elaborate on conversion drivers and sustainability given capex scrutiny?

Michael Reynolds:
Great question, David. The 92% demo conversion from our Accelerator Program is key, bundling training and guarantees. Sustainability comes from higher EBITDA lifts—15-20%—and reimbursements like $8,500 hysterectomies. FlexLease covers 40%, and utilization surpassing hospitals at 18.2 procedures ensures annuity revenue. We see 75% year-end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter - Goldman Sachs:
Jennifer, your Q4 revenue guide raised—how does mix and FX factor in, and op margin drivers?

Jennifer Hale:
Emily, the raise reflects U.S. electives and EvoFlow ramp, 9-14% organic. Consumables 66%+ mix adds 75% margins. FX $50M FY headwind. Op margin to 24.5-25.5% from $25M SG&A savings, digital sales, R&D gains—200bps YoY.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim - Morgan Stanley:
Raj, exciting R&D pipeline—timeline risks for EvoFlow data and competition in robotics?

Raj Patel:
Robert, Q1 2025 topline on track, 98% success low risk. Robotics AI module Phase II $40M protects vs. Stryker Mako, with 25% time savings. Our 16% CAGR R&D outpaces, genomics partnerships boost outcomes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Anna Patel - Bank of America:
Lisa, commercial thoughts on organic growth in APAC 11.4% and share gains vs. Intuitive?

Lisa Chen:
Anna, APAC led by China NMPA, Japan approvals, 16% China growth. Share from Intuitive via 15% lower costs, 98.7% uptime—62% head-to-head wins. Precision360 digital lifts productivity, targeting 70% consumables mix.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
